test.connectDescription: Connect to the mounted tool to move its joints by hand and to test its servo bus. Possible without the robot module.
test.connectBody: Once connected, the jog buttons, the joint sliders of the mounted tool and the bus tests move the real tool. Before you continue, check that:
test.routineTestRunning: A routine test is running on the tool: stop it first.
test.sliderLinked: Connected: the sliders move the real tool, and the model follows its measured position.
test.sliderFollowOnly: Connected: the model follows the measured position. Moving the tool is not allowed right now.
test.sliderOtherTool: The mounted tool is “{mounted}”: these sliders only move the model.

diag.jointMoves: The joint moves: it sweeps over ±80 % of its range at 30 °/s and returns home at the end. Keep clear of the tool.
diag.runAllHint: Runs the four tests one after the other, each for the selected duration, and then says in one sentence what the pattern of failures points at. The joint moves during the last two. This is the run to send when reporting a bus fault.

failureMeans.idle: The fault is there even with nothing happening on the bus: look at the wiring, the connector, the USB adapter or the baud rate. The other tests cannot be judged until this one is clean.
failureMeans.traffic: With no motion there is no motor current, so the cause is the timing on the bus: a read sent right behind a command meets that command's acknowledgement. This is fixed in software.
failureMeans.motion_spaced: The reads are kept apart from the commands, so timing is ruled out: the cause is electrical – a supply dip, motor noise, or the cable flexing with the joint.
failureMeans.motion: This is what a routine does. Compare with the two tests before: failures only here mean bus timing made worse by motion; failures in “spaced reads” too mean an electrical cause.

diag.title: Servo bus diagnostics
diag.description: Counts the failed position reads in four situations, to tell a bus timing fault from an electrical one. The two motion tests sweep the joint over ±80 % of its range at 30 °/s and bring it home.

scenarioHint.idle: Position reads only, no command: checks wiring, adapter and baud rate.
scenarioHint.traffic: Commands at the routine's rate to the same position (no motion), with reads right behind them: checks the bus timing.
scenarioHint.motion_spaced: The joint sweeps; each read waits for the bus to be quiet: checks power, noise and cable.
scenarioHint.motion: The joint sweeps with reads right behind the commands, as a routine does.

hint.IDLE: The system is waiting for a cycle start. Entering test mode locks the cycle until you leave it.
hint.BUSY: The system is starting up, homing or running a cycle. Test mode is available once it is idle.
hint.TEST: Test mode: the cycle is locked and start triggers are ignored. Leaving brings the tool home and restarts the system from its initial state.
hint.UNKNOWN: The robotics orchestrator is not running, so test mode cannot be entered.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The end-effector test node does not answer. Check that the robotics stack is running on this machine.

test.exitForceHint: Leaves test mode even though the tool could not be brought home. Check the tool before starting a cycle.
test.noServos: Nothing to move on this tool:
test.jogHint: Click for one step, hold to keep moving

hansen: Hansen is one of the most recognized brands of quick-connect couplings for hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

Its design is so standard within the industry that the term "Hansen-style connector" or "Hansen profile" is often used generically to describe this specific type of coupling, regardless of the manufacturer.

Currently, the Hansen coupling line belongs to Danfoss (following its acquisition of Eaton’s hydraulics division); consequently, it is very common to find these connectors marketed under the names Eaton-Hansen or Danfoss.

live.title: Real end effector
live.description: Run the displayed routine on the mounted tool alone, without the robot: a test of the communication with the end effector and of its motion.
live.ready: Ready: press play to run the selected target's routine on the tool.
live.running: Running the routine of target {target} on the tool.

hint.IDLE: The robot module is running and idle. Enter test mode to lock the cycle; the test is allowed only then.
hint.BUSY: The system is starting up, homing or running a cycle. No test is possible now.
hint.TEST: Test mode: the cycle is locked. The tool can be tested.
hint.UNKNOWN: The robot module is not running. The tool can be tested on its own.
hint.UNREACHABLE: The end-effector module does not answer. Check that ee_app is running on this machine.

block.unreachable: The end-effector module does not answer.
block.toolMismatch: The mounted tool is "{mounted}": select it to test it.
block.oldNode: The running end-effector module does not offer the routine test (update ee_app).
block.needTestMode: The robot module is running: enter test mode first.
block.selectTarget: Select one target: the test runs one routine at a time.
block.busy: The robot module is busy (starting up, homing or running a cycle).

override.label: Bypass the robot state check
override.hint: Run the test whatever the robot module is doing, e.g. while the robot is still being set up. Safety is then your responsibility.
override.active: Bypass active: the test runs in any system state. Nothing prevents the robot from moving meanwhile.
override.confirmBody: The test is normally refused while the robot module is busy, and needs test mode while it is idle, so that the robot and the tool are never commanded at the same time. With the bypass the tool can be tested in any state:
override.robotMayMove: the robot may move, start a cycle or home while the tool is moving;
override.cycleNotLocked: the cycle is not locked, and a cycle that reaches a target routine during the test will fail;
override.responsibility: keeping people, the part and the robot clear of the tool is entirely your responsibility.

confirm.title: The real end effector will move
confirm.body: Once connected, the play button runs the routine on the mounted tool instead of only simulating it. Before you continue, check that:
confirm.robotStill: the robot is stationary and will not be moved meanwhile;
confirm.toolClear: the tool is clear of the part, of people and of any obstacle over its whole travel;
confirm.noCompensation: you expect the tip to swing: the robot does not compensate the tool's motion in this test.
